dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Confirmed real incident: auto-publish.json's first 3 hourly runs (Sep 25, 15:00-17:00 UTC) all failed silently on a 401 and nobody noticed short of manually opening the tracker — there is no signal today for either a failed run or an empty queue.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: User confirmed two measurable outcomes: (1) a daily email arrives and accurately reflects tracker state (next queued item, or nothing queued), replacing manual tracker checks; (2) a pipeline failure is surfaced within ~1h via an immediate alert (the next hourly auto-publish run), not just by the next daily digest.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: User approved the 10-item pass/fail list below covering domain verification, credential hygiene, docs, the digest workflow, the failure-alert branch, and the web/app.py no-change constraint — each paired with a cmd or an explicitly named judgment check.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: User confirmed in-scope (Resend domain+key setup, cross-project docs, daily digest workflow, failure-alert branch in auto-publish.json, HTML-formatted emails) and out-of-scope (multi-recipient support, a general notifications framework, any change to the Instagram publish step itself).

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Surfaced tension between 'near-real-time failure alerts' and 'don't risk the already-fragile live auto-publish workflow' — user explicitly chose to accept the risk and edit auto-publish.json additively, resolving the contradiction rather than leaving it implicit.

problem: The Pancracio auto-publish pipeline (n8n/workflows/auto-publish.json, running hourly against pancracio-ideas.santiagomorel.dev) has no failure or status visibility outside the tracker UI. On 2026-09-25 its first 3 hourly executions (15:00, 16:00, 17:00 UTC) all failed with a silent 401 on the old Basic Auth credential — nobody noticed because nothing surfaces pipeline state anywhere. The only way to know whether anything is queued, about to publish, or has failed is to manually open the tracker.

Separately, there is no reusable email-sending setup for santiagomorel.dev at all — zero mail-related DNS records exist today. Every future project on this domain would otherwise have to re-derive domain verification and API-key strategy from scratch.
goals: A daily email (9am UTC, from a verified santiagomorel.dev subdomain) arrives without fail and accurately reflects the tracker's real state: either 'nothing queued' or the next auto-publish item's title/quote/scheduled time.
A pipeline failure is surfaced within ~1 hour via its own immediate alert email, rather than waiting up to 24h for the next daily digest.

The Resend domain verification and API-key pattern are documented in porfolio/internal-docs/ (the repo that actually serves santiagomorel.dev) so a future, unrelated project can reuse them without re-deriving anything.
Both the digest and alert emails render as styled HTML rather than plain text.

decisions.decision: One ideation project with two/three sequenced phases, not two separate ideation contracts
decisions.rejected: Splitting the general Resend setup and the Pancracio digest into two separate ideation projects
decisions.reason: The digest phase has a hard dependency on the Resend phase, and the combined scope is small enough that two contracts would mostly duplicate ceremony.

decisions.decision: Verify a dedicated subdomain (notify.santiagomorel.dev) with Resend
decisions.rejected: Verifying the bare santiagomorel.dev root domain
decisions.reason: Isolates transactional-email sending reputation from the root domain (which also serves the portfolio site), and matches the account's existing convention of one subdomain per service (bulbasaur.*, pancracio-ideas.*).

decisions.decision: One Resend API key per project
decisions.rejected: A single shared account-wide API key reused across all future projects
decisions.reason: Matches the account's existing per-service credential pattern (separate n8n read/write keys, per-project bearer tokens); smaller blast radius if one key leaks or needs rotating.

decisions.decision: Document the general Resend setup in porfolio/internal-docs/
decisions.reason: porfolio is the actual repo serving santiagomorel.dev and already holds this domain's other infra notes (deployment-notes.md, internal-info.md) — confirmed by reading its nginx config, which shows it deploys to /var/www/profile on the box serving santiagomorel.dev.

decisions.decision: Send via a plain n8n HTTP Request node calling Resend's REST API, authenticated with an httpHeaderAuth credential
decisions.reason: Confirmed by direct inspection (SSH into the n8n VPS, n8n v2.40.6): no Resend node ships in this n8n install. Matches the exact shape already used by the 'Pancracio Tracker Bearer Token' credential.

decisions.decision: No new backend endpoint for failure/status data
decisions.reason: Confirmed by reading web/app.py: _run_auto_publish_pipeline already sets status='failed' on any exception, so the existing /api/ideas?status=failed (and ?auto_publish=true) already expose everything both emails need.

decisions.decision: Add an immediate failure-alert branch directly to auto-publish.json, accepting the risk of editing a live, already-fragile production workflow
decisions.rejected: Keep auto-publish.json untouched and only surface failures via the next daily digest (worst case ~24h)
decisions.reason: User explicitly prioritized faster failure detection (~1h, the next hourly run) over the lower-risk option, given the Sep 25 incident already went unnoticed for hours; the edit is additive (a new branch after the existing HTTP node), not a change to existing logic.
User wants the digest and alert emails to look nicer than plain text.

decisions.decision: The daily digest workflow reports queue state only (nothing-queued vs. next-up); failure visibility stays exclusively the alert branch's job
decisions.rejected: Also having the digest's Code node check /api/ideas?status=failed for the last 24h
decisions.reason: Plan-critic review (scope-creep and over-engineering lenses, independently) flagged that the failed-item check traced to no stated goal or success criterion, duplicated the dedicated Full-tier alert branch, and edged into the explicitly-deferred 'richer pipeline-health content' future item — removed rather than promoted, since goal 2's ~1h alert already covers failure visibility faster than a daily check could.

phases.title: General Resend Setup
phases.notes: Verify notify.santiagomorel.dev with Resend (DNS records on santiagomorel.dev, DigitalOcean-hosted nameservers), create a Pancracio-scoped API key, create the matching n8n httpHeaderAuth credential live via n8n's REST API (never committed to git, per this project's established credential pattern), and write the reusable setup doc in porfolio/internal-docs/. Blocks both other phases — nothing can send email until this exists. DNS propagation and Resend's own verification step are live, external-system steps that can't be completed inside a local build session; the spec must name them as an explicit manual/live step, per this project's own recorded learning about phases that depend on live deployments or external credentials. Two prerequisites to name explicitly in the spec: (1) adding the DNS records needs DigitalOcean console/API access for santiagomorel.dev — not yet documented anywhere in internal-docs/credentials/, unlike every other external credential this project uses; (2) creating the n8n credential needs a write-scoped n8n API key — the only one that exists (`pancracio-auto-publish-workflow-mgmt`) expires 2026-10-25, so if this phase starts after that date a fresh write-scoped key must be generated first.

phases.title: Daily Digest Workflow
phases.notes: New n8n/workflows/pancracio-digest.json: daily schedule trigger (9am UTC) -> HTTP GET /api/ideas?auto_publish=true (reusing the existing 'Pancracio Tracker Bearer Token' credential) -> Code node to determine 'nothing queued' vs. next-up -> HTTP POST to Resend with an HTML body. Scoped to queue state only — failure reporting is Phase 3's job, not duplicated here. Independent of Phase 3; both only depend on Phase 1.

phases.title: Failure Alert Branch
phases.notes: Additive branch on the existing, live auto-publish.json: after 'Run Pipeline For Idea' (which already sets onError: continueRegularOutput), add a check for a failed/error item and an HTTP POST to Resend when one is found. Before building the branch, verify in the n8n UI what a real errored execution's output item actually looks like under continueRegularOutput — specifically whether the idea's id/title survive on the errored item or need to be recovered from the earlier 'Split Into Ideas' item — since the branch's ability to name which idea failed depends on it. Must be applied via n8n's REST API against the live instance (same pattern as the bearer-credential swap, commit fd075e6) and the exported JSON re-committed to match — this is a live-deployment-dependent step per this project's own recorded learning, not something a local build can complete or verify end-to-end on its own.
